what_it_does: Running a large language model (an AI like a chatbot) on a server actually involves two very different jobs: first, digesting the user's prompt all at once (called the prefill phase, which is very compute-heavy), and then generating the reply one word at a time (called the decoding phase, which is limited by how fast data can be read from memory). Current server setups use the same fixed hardware for both jobs even though they have opposite needs, which wastes resources and drives up cost. LLMShare builds a simulator that models how different hardware options — ordinary server CPUs, graphics cards (GPUs), and specialized AI accelerators — would perform and cost money for each phase separately. It then searches that space to find the best mix of hardware for each phase, matching capability to demand.
